claim: Soar raises typed impasses (no operator, tie, conflict, operator no-change); each starts a substate that reuses the same decision loop.
agent_test: Compare typed triggers (nothing to try, many options, chosen option stalls) against one generic stuck trigger on the same items at equal tokens.
audit_note: Laird text names three types, glossary four; claim lists four, fine. Evidence a01/a02/a19/b06 are the same paper (one source), but the manual independently supports the substate/chunk mechanism.

claim: Chunking stores only what the substate actually used as conditions; this implicit generalisation is what makes a chunk reusable. A representation that bundles roles in one slot makes chunks too specific.
agent_test: Store full-context vs used-facts-only triggers for subgoal entries; measure reuse hit rate on held-out items.
audit_note: 1986 paper (full text) and Laird 2022 support; Soar Manual notes EBBS (9.6) replaced old chunking for over-specialization, so implicit-generalization is the classic mechanism; minor.

claim: Chunking cuts steps in every tested toy task but total time rose in 4 of 8 (total speedup: Eight-puzzle about 0.99, 2-Queens 0.32, Grid 0.85, Magic-square 0.25; per-step cost up to 25x) because a few chunks are expensive to match. Fewer steps does not mean less cost.
agent_test: Log total tokens and latency including retrieval for a library vs no library; cap entries retrieved per state.
audit_note: All numbers match Tambe, Newell & Rosenbloom 1990 Table 1 (total speedups 0.99/0.32/0.85/0.25; 25x), but every supporting evidence line is that single paper (the Dynamic Cheatsheet line does not bear on the claim); only one independent source.

claim: Cheap-to-match restricted stored formats bound cost but need more entries to reach equal coverage; extra training trials for the restricted version were hand-picked.
agent_test: Compare strict-schema triggers vs free-text triggers on cost and coverage.

claim: Over-specific learned rules multiply: one arithmetic agent learned 1263 rules under old chunking and 8 under EBBS (Soar 9.6). A library needs generalise-and-merge.
agent_test: Measure the near-duplicate rate of auto-saved entries and merge them; test reuse before and after merging.

claim: A stored subgoal result is only correct if replaying the substate would give the same result; Soar has no general mechanism to delete a bad chunk, and chunking needs deterministic substate decisions.
agent_test: Admit an entry only after a code check; re-run the check at reuse; demote entries that match then fail.

claim: Chunking is a form of explanation-based learning and can encode unverified guesses as beliefs when the domain theory is not fully believed.
agent_test: Inject a wrong but plausible subgoal result and see whether an ungated library propagates it.

claim: The power law of practice that chunking theory was built to explain is contested: unaveraged data favour an exponential (7,910 series, 475 subjects, 24 experiments); the chunking authors' own refit for one Seibel subject also favoured exponential (secondhand).
agent_test: Fit gain-per-entry curves directly; do not assume a functional form.

claim: The original chunking model's learning rate is a free parameter (p=0.01) and the long curve came from a meta-model; it is a demonstration, not a fit to human data.
agent_test: Treat admission thresholds as tuned knobs; sweep them.

claim: Founding transfer demonstration: Eight Puzzle macro table in 61 chunks with all three transfer types (83 without across-column symmetry, 230 with no transfer); Tower of Hanoi 3 disks in 8 chunks. Hand-designed representation and hand-picked trials.
agent_test: Count entries needed for coverage with and without separable state descriptions.

claim: Curated procedural skills raise LLM agent pass rate (33.9% to 50.5%, +16.6 pp, 87 tasks, 18 configs, 9,396 trajectories); a 30-task partial replication found +24.7 to +36.0 pp for two models.
agent_test: Compare no library vs vetted library at equal tokens on our benchmark slice.
audit_note: Numbers match SkillsBench (87 tasks, 18 configs, 9,396 trajectories, 33.9->50.5) and Xu & Wu (curated +36.0 GPT-5.5, +24.7 DeepSeek). The replication is on a subset of the same benchmark by different authors.

claim: Model-written skills authored before the task do not help and usually hurt: -8.1 to -11.5 pp on three configs in the final SkillsBench; an earlier version cited by surveys reported -1.3 pp average. Not a direct test of impasse-triggered chunking.
agent_test: Compare auto-saved vs test-gated entries; expect auto-saved to be worse. The two SkillsBench versions disagree on size.

claim: Fewer, shorter skills work better: 1 skill +18.0 pp, 2-3 +19.0, 4+ +10.1; compact +19.0 vs comprehensive +0.7 pp. Skills hurt on 13 of 87 tasks, where they act as a fixed pipeline with no applicability condition.
agent_test: Cap retrieved entries per state at 1-3 and keep entries short; test 1, 3, 6.

claim: Skill availability matters more than presentation detail: low vs high abstraction changed results by +0.7 and -6.7 pp, both CIs crossing zero.
agent_test: Fix retrieval first; vary wording later.

claim: Stored abstractions (rules, summaries, skills) can carry errors forward: raw trajectory memory beat abstraction memory (53.5 vs 49.0 mean success over 9 settings) and the authors' anti-persistence method reached 59.9. Authors' own method, 3 seeds.
agent_test: Store case plus checked outcome vs distilled rule per entry; compare success and repeated-error rate.

claim: Retrieval memories collide: similar queries needing different workflows pull foreign items (at position 200 of a compound stream, 52% of BFCL-Miss and 46% of BFCL-Base episodes retrieve a memory from the opposite workflow); separately, a prompt-rewriting method (GEPA) cut its clarification rate on BFCL-Miss from 29.8% to 11.2% after training on BFCL-Base, losing earlier-learned behaviour.
agent_test: Scope entries to trigger; test collision rate on near-duplicate tasks needing different fixes.
audit_note: 52%/46% are right (Chen et al. 2026, ReasoningBank, position 200 of compound drift), but 29.8%->11.2% is GEPA's clarification rate on BFCL-Miss after the BFCL-Base block (119/400 to 45/400), not a pass/accuracy rate on BFCL-Base, and it is a rewriting-interference result, not a retrieval collision.
claim_before_audit: Retrieval memories collide: similar queries needing different workflows pull foreign items (52% and 46% foreign late in a compound stream); a rewriting method fell from 29.8% to 11.2% on BFCL-Base.

claim: Workflows compiled from past successes raise web-agent success (WebArena 35.5 vs 23.5, +12.0 pp, +51.1% relative; about 2 fewer steps); gains depend on template overlap, yet online AWM kept an 8.9 to 14.0 pp edge as the train-test gap widened.
agent_test: Split test items into in-template and new-structure; report library gain on each.

claim: Keeping both a rule-like insight and a retrieved worked example beats either alone in some tasks; which matters more is task dependent (ALFWorld put: ReAct 50, insights 61, retrieve 73, ExpeL 83).
agent_test: Entry = short rule plus one worked example; ablate each.

claim: A rule-based maintenance layer for a skill library helps (SkillOps, ALFWorld 79.5%, +8.8 pp over strongest baseline).
agent_test: Add a program-run retire/merge/re-test step and compare to a growing library.

claim: LLM output used at an impasse should be verified before compiling: GPT-3 goal proposals were accepted 30-40% by a human and Search+LLM without review completed 54% of subtasks; a later Soar-LLM position paper reports over 70% of responses not viable.
agent_test: Measure acceptance rate of model-proposed subgoal results under a code check; store only passed ones.
audit_note: Kirk et al. 2022 (54%, 30-40%) and Kirk/Wray/Laird 2023 (>70% not viable) verified; both are the same Soar group, so the 'later position paper' is not independent of the first, but the claim itself says so.

claim: The impasse-to-LLM-to-chunk loop cuts later LLM calls in a recommender (CogRec: call frequency falls to a plateau with chunking, stays high without), but the accuracy gain over Soar alone is modest (ML-1M HR@10 0.3124 vs 0.2956, +5.7%) and there is no outside replication. The text confirms the three ablations (no bootstrap, no chunking, no Soar) and a call-frequency plateau; plateau point is only in a figure.
agent_test: Track model calls per task as the library fills; a falling curve is expected, flat means compilation is failing.

claim: An execution-grounded critic is the key part when an LLM writes Soar rules: removing it cut success by 23%; framework 86-91% vs one-shot 55-66% on 100 water-jug cases; decision cycles 1.76-1.98x optimal vs manual about 3390x. One domain, models differ between arms.
agent_test: Revise stored entries from real execution output; ablate the critic at equal tokens.

claim: Scoped retry did better than whole-trial retry in these comparisons: ADaPT (retries only the failed subtask via recursive decomposition) beat Reflexion 71.6 vs 57.5 (ALFWorld), 44.0 vs 35.0 (WebShop), 52.0 vs 32.0 (TextCraft) with GPT-3.5, though the ADaPT authors only hypothesise that retry scope is the cause; in GraSP, full GraSP with local repair scored 80.6 vs 77.4 with global replanning on ALFWorld.
agent_test: Subgoal on the failed step only vs restart the whole attempt at equal tokens.
audit_note: ADaPT and GraSP numbers are real, but ADaPT vs Reflexion differs in recursive planner decomposition, not only retry scope (authors only hypothesise the cause), and the GraSP 79.7 is the partial '+Local Repair' ablation row, whereas the matched comparison is full GraSP 80.6 vs global replan 77.4.
claim_before_audit: Retry scoped to the failed part beats whole-trial retry: ADaPT 71.6 vs Reflexion 57.5 (ALFWorld), 44.0 vs 35.0 (WebShop), 52.0 vs 32.0 (TextCraft), GPT-3.5, ADaPT authors' own runs; GraSP local repair 79.7 vs global replan 77.4 (ALFWorld).

claim: As-needed decomposition (decompose only when the executor fails) beat plan-then-execute in ADaPT (ALFWorld 71.6 vs 43.3).
agent_test: Trigger subgoal only on failure vs always plan first, equal tokens.

claim: No current LLM agent has the full Soar chain (typed impasse, protected substate, typed return, compiled chunk); a 2026 review lists failure conditions: misdiagnosis, unsafe compile, parent-state corruption, no drop in repeat failures.
agent_test: Use the four listed failure conditions as test cases; the gap claim is a review judgement, not measured.

claim: Failure diagnosis is often wrong at the exact step (AgentDebugX strict attribution 28.8%); typed failure to retrieved recovery works with training (PALADIN, recovery up to 89.68% vs CRITIC 76.34%).
agent_test: Do not compile a recovery from a diagnosis alone; require a passing re-run.
audit_note: Both verified (AgentDebugX Who&When strict agent+step 28.8% vs 21.7%, qwen3.5-9b; PALADIN RR 89.68% vs CRITIC 76.34%); note 28.8% is for the authors' own best method on a 9B model, so 'often wrong' is conservative.

claim: Compiling subgoals into a trained policy degrades less than baselines under compositional goals (HERAKLES -51% vs -64% to -92% at n=4). Needs training; not a scaffold result.
agent_test: Out of scope for a frozen-model scaffold.

claim: A verification gate before admitting an entry raises downstream success at the same induction budget: ASI shopping site 32.6 (unverified text) to 36.4 (verified program, in memory) and 39.0 (verified text); the gate admitted 15.6% of turns versus 31.4% for the ungated method.
agent_test: Same trigger, gated vs ungated library at equal tokens on reasoning items.

claim: Memory-addition gate strength matters (Xiong et al. 2025, four agents): add-all and an off-the-shelf LLM-judge (coarse) filter let errors accumulate and widened the gap to an error-free-memory variant, whereas strict (human-grade) selection let AgentDriver close and pass that gap after ~2000 executions; a coarse judge fine-tuned on 300 trajectories also improved over time. Agents copy retrieved records when inputs are similar (experience-following).
agent_test: Compare ungated, LLM-judge and code-check gates; count repeated errors.
audit_note: Xiong et al. show add-all and the untuned coarse evaluator (C1) widen the gap to error-free memory, but some coarse evaluators (e.g. one fine-tuned on 300 trajectories) improved over time, and the strict-selection result (catching up to and passing error-free after ~2000 executions) is shown for AgentDriver only; the claim is also single-paper (Dynamic Cheatsheet lines only loosely support error clustering).
claim_before_audit: Gate strength matters: strict selection kept memory close to an error-free memory, while add-all and coarse LLM-judge selection widened the gap and propagated errors (four agents). Agents copy retrieved records when inputs are similar.

claim: Demotion by use is measured: delete a record after n retrievals when its mean downstream utility is under a threshold. It helps with a reliable judge and hurts with a coarse one; combined with age-based deletion it gives the best size/performance balance.
agent_test: Count entry uses and post-use outcomes; demote after n uses below threshold; compare to a growing library.

claim: In Voyager, removing self-verification cost more discovered items (-73%) than a missing library, whose effect shows at later tiers (iron 21 vs 29 iterations, diamond 1/3 vs 0/3) and in transfer (18-21 vs 26-36 iterations); library retrieval top-5 accuracy 96.5%. Verification also steers retry, so it is not a pure gate.
agent_test: Separate gate from retry control in our ablation.

claim: On reasoning tasks, curated libraries help but uncurated accumulation can fall below baseline: Dynamic Cheatsheet Sonnet AIME 2024 23.3 to 50.0 (curated) vs 26.7 (append everything), GPT-4o 20.0 to 6.7 under append-everything; small models gain little. LEGO-Prover verified lemma library +3.3 points (50.4 vs 47.1), gap widening as the library grows.
agent_test: Run curated vs append-all library at equal tokens on a 100+ item reasoning slice (AIME sets of 30 are too small).
audit_note: Dynamic Cheatsheet (Sonnet AIME24 23.3->50.0 DC vs 26.7 FH; GPT-4o 20.0->6.7 FH) and LEGO-Prover (50.4 vs 47.1, gap widens) verified in the papers; sources are independent.

claim: Distilling lessons from failed attempts helps only with a distilling method: ReasoningBank WebArena 48.8 vs AWM 44.1 vs none 40.5 (Gemini-2.5-flash); failures added 3.2 points for ReasoningBank (46.5 to 49.7) but only 1.1 for Synapse; AWM fell below no-memory for Claude-3.7 (40.8 vs 41.7). This conflicts with the finding that raw cases beat abstractions (K15).
agent_test: Case vs distilled-rule entries, same gate, same retrieval.

claim: No published ablation separates an impasse-type trigger from a generic stuck trigger. The closest, a 5-low-progress-step gate (DPR), reports no gate-vs-schedule comparison on the page read.
agent_test: Typed triggers vs one stuck trigger on same items.
